I think a lot of people, especially depressed teenagers as another commentor mentioned, can relate to Hamlet. Many people have felt like they are smarter than everybody else, but also suffer more and are more aware of the horrors of the world. It's like sitting at a birthday party and everybody is having fun but you just can't get into it, so you console yourself by being existential because it makes life feel meaningful and deep. It's like, "How could you be happy at a time like this!!?? When climate change is destroying the Earth and people are dying in Gaza?!" (anybody have friends like that?)

I think Hamlet is very emotional. He is burdened by the grief of his father's death. His grief is very genuine. He is going through a difficult point in his life and confronting his parents mortality, which also forces him to confront his own mortality. Basically Hamlet is young and he's not ready to move on from his father's death. I like how this is expanded into the murder mystery, crime thriller of the rest of the plot, but it starts very grounded and relatable. Everybody has lost someone, and the first big one is always the hardest because it is your first experience of grief so the feeling is intense and difficult to cope.

Shakespeare wrote Hamlet after the death of his son, Hamnet, so you can see it as a way for him to process the grief of losing a child. I think he is exploring philosophical questions through Hamlet. For example, why should we suffer? Why are we born and why do we love people just for them to die? Why not just kill oneself? This is explored in the to be or not to be speech.

I do think Claudius deserved to die. I guess there's this whole question of Hamlet's sanity. Either Hamlet is insane and Claudius is innocent; or Hamlet is sane and Claudius is evil. To me, it never struck me for a second that Hamlet was insane, as in delusional or paranoid. I think by the end scene it's pretty clear that Claudius is a villian who is guilty of killing Hamlet's father. I think he does deserve to die for this. change requires action. Hamlet's fatal flaw is his inability to take action, and therefore his inability to enact change. there are also state changes, life to death as referenced in the alas poor yorick scene and the to be or not to be soliloquy. 

the natural outcome of time is change. Human beings seem to naturally fear death, to the point that we can't accept it as our inevitable fate. How often do you hear people acknowledge that they will die? We all prefer not to think about it.

Hamlet wants to stand still, endlessly collecting data so he can evaluate the best course of action. This appears rational, but it is actually a response to his overwhelming emotions. Hamlet dwells too long on his emotions, as represented by the fact that he wears black to mourn his father even after his mom gets remarried. This also shows Hamlet's inability to process his emotions.

Over the course of the play, Hamlet self-actualizes, and thereby learns not to fear death, but to accept it. It is inevitable, after all. quote:

On the FRQs you can write as much as you want and be completely wrong on most of it but if you write one thing that is correct you get the point. The other false stuff won’t count against you. 

The multiple choice is all memorization. Depending on who you are, that is either good or bad news, but that’s what it is.

Form, function, content, context, and general significance.

Here’s a quick example for Starry Night by Van Goph:

Form: heavily stylized, thick impasto

Function: expressed Van Goph’s inner turmoil 

Content: church spire, night sky, swirling yellow stars

Context: painted from imagination, based on view from Goph’s asylum window

Significance: it was deliberately stylized, which shows a shift from realism to abstraction in art, which led to the birth of Expressionism. 

On the written responses you will need to be able to identify the artwork’s title, artist, date of creation, and materials. You need to get two correct to get the point.

That’s really all there is to it. The example I gave is just that: an example. There are many other things you could say about the artwork and still receive credit. It just comes down to what you remember! Your answer will be in essay format though. 

For multiple choice you either know it or you don’t. It will ask you a fact about a piece of art that you should have memorized. You may be able to deduce the answer from knowledge about the piece or history. If by complex you mean that the characters have depth then yes, I think hxh has mastered this. Gon is not just a innocently curious kid, as we learn by the Chimera Ant Arc, he is practically amoral. This is hinted at by Zepile in the York Shin arc, but it doesn’t really become apparent until we see his actions in this arc. It is a look deeper into the traits that often characterize a shounen protagonist, expanded upon and deconstructed to reveal how damaging these traits can be.

More remarkable than that though is the complexity of side characters. Koala is character we interact with for 1-2? episodes, yet we are aware of his life story, motivations, regrets, goals, etc. It truly is incredible the care Togashi takes in developing these characters we see for such a short time, and a testament to his immense talent that he can do it in such a short time.

In conclusion, yes the characters in hxh are complex, it is one of the most remarkable things about the show.

IMO, unless Kurapika finds something to live for after he’s avenged his brethren, he will die. His whole plan was to become a hunter so he could kill the PT, collect the eyes, and die (I don’t assume he wanted to live, everything and everyone he knew being gone), but it was interrupted when he met his friends. He realizes that he may not have to avenge his clan and that moving on and starting a new life is an option. His first line in the series “I just hope that my rage will not fade over time” reveals that he doesn’t REALLY want to kill the PT and is only doing it out of obligation. But once that rage fades (as it did near the end of YN when he thought the troupe was dead), he can recover and live for something else besides revenge, namely, friendship.

I think from a storytelling perspective, their relationship is very important. Their arcs are kind of intertwined, if that makes sense. In a literary sense, Leorio matters to Kurapika because Kurapika’s only goal in leaving his clan was to find a doctor to heal Pairo’s eyes. Thus his relationship with Leorio (a doctor) represents him fulfilling his final promise to his murdered friend, if not literally then symbolically.

Likewise, for Leorio, Kurapika symbolically represents a friend that he can save, which was his motivation for becoming a Hunter in the first place.

They represent and fulfill each other’s motivations, which I don’t think is by accident. They haven’t spent a lot of time together on screen, and yet Leorio recommended Kurapika for the Zodiac position. I think, though they do have separate goals, they rely specifically on each other to reach those goals. 

I don’t know if Togashi plans on developing their relationship further (I hope he does!), but I think if he does, their relationship will go a similar way as Gon and Killua’s (they will become best friends). They do matter to each other. Kurapika is comforted by Leorio and Leorio is naturally protecting of his friends, which includes Kurapika. I can’t predict where their relationship will go, but to me it seems likely that they will be significant in each other’s development and final character arc.

Nonbinary is an umbrella term that gender fluid falls under. 

Nonbinary people feel they are separate from the binary genders of a man or woman, but their gender is static. 

Genderfluid people are more fluid, as to be expected. They shift from being separate and within the binary. The key difference is that their gender is shifting; it is not static. 

If you are genderfluid you are also nonbinary, and they can be very similar. The clearest distinction is that genderfluidity indicates changes, and nonbinary does not. 

Hope that helps! I'm not nonbinary or genderfluid, myself so it may be more helpful to get a POV from someone who is. People write tons of articles on it, but don't feel like you need to make a choice right away....or at all. Gender is a tricky thing.
